title: Photosynthesis: The Light Reactions
text: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. Light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll and other pigments in two photosystems: Photosystem II and Photosystem I. In Photosystem II, water molecules are split (photolysis) to release oxygen, protons, and electrons. The electrons travel through the electron transport chain, generating a proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis by ATP synthase. In Photosystem I, electrons are re-energized by light and ultimately used to reduce NADP+ to NADPH. The ATP and NADPH produced power the Calvin cycle, which occurs in the stroma.
